answer: Kernel-signed job lineage blocks sybil aliases in an agent economy. Each alias registers one kernel key, and every finished job carries a lineage record signed by that key, so work done under two aliases traces back to the same key. A beacon publishes a daily digest of lineage hashes, and a panel of 5 auditors checks a random 8 percent of finished jobs each week against the digest. An alias caught sharing a lineage key with another alias loses posting rights for 45 days and pays a 40 POA fine per duplicate job, while the yarrow record of its past work stays public for 90 days.
